cards.text: Israel is camped in the plains of Moab along the Jordan, across from Jericho (Numbers 22:1). The Reubenites and the Gadites, two of Israel's tribes, have very large herds and flocks, and I mean SO many animals, friend. So they take a good long look at the lands of Jazer and Gilead.

cards.question: The Reubenites and Gadites look over Jazer and Gilead. They see the region is suitable for ___.

cards.text: So they go to Moses, Israel's leader, along with Eleazar the priest and the leaders, and rattle off nine towns the LORD conquered, all good for livestock, and hey, they just happen to have livestock. That's not a conversation, friend, that's a REAL ESTATE TOUR.

cards.question: The Gadites and Reubenites start with, "If we have found favor in your sight," and then comes the big ask. What is it?

answers.text: Let them keep this land instead of crossing
Let them have more of the war spoil
Let them take the best land in Canaan

cards.question: Moses loves the plan from the Gadites and Reubenites and says yes right away.

cards.text: Moses asks them, "Shall your brothers go to war while you sit here?" Oh, so you're the friend who "helps" with the big move by holding the door OPEN.

cards.question: Moses has a second question for the Gadites and Reubenites. What does he say they're doing to the rest of Israel?

answers.text: Taking the best pasture for themselves

cards.question: Moses says he's seen this move before. Who does he say did it?

cards.text: Back at Kadesh-barnea, Moses sent their fathers to inspect the land, and at the Valley of Eshcol they saw it and discouraged the Israelites from going in. That's a one-star review, friend, and the WHOLE camp read it.

cards.question: Back then, after their fathers discouraged Israel, the LORD's anger was kindled and He swore an oath.
In His oath, the LORD says the men who came out of Egypt won't see the land. Which men?
The LORD's oath has two exceptions: ___ son of Jephunneh and ___ son of Nun.

cards.text: Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun followed the LORD wholeheartedly, so they get in. Out of that whole generation, friend, TWO names, and that tells you how much wholehearted matters.

cards.question: How long does the LORD make Israel wander in the wilderness, until that whole generation is gone?

cards.text: Now Moses calls them "a brood of sinners," risen up in place of their fathers to stoke the LORD's anger even more. Moses did NOT put that one in a cookie box with a little bow on top.

cards.question: Moses warns the Gadites and Reubenites: if they turn away from following the LORD, He will leave Israel in the ___ again.

cards.text: Moses ends with, "you will be the cause of their destruction." So the Gadites and Reubenites come back with a new plan, sheepfolds here for the livestock and cities for their little ones, and okay, okay, I SEE you, Plan B.

cards.question: Plan B from the Gadites and Reubenites has one more part. Their men will ___ themselves and go ahead of the Israelites.
The Gadites and Reubenites promise not to go home until every Israelite has taken his inheritance.

cards.text: And they won't take an inheritance across the Jordan with everyone else, because theirs has come to them on the east side. Their minds are made up, friend. They are DONE house hunting.
Moses answers with a big IF. If they arm themselves before the LORD for battle, and every armed man crosses the Jordan until He has driven His enemies out...

cards.question: If the Gadites and Reubenites do all that and the land is subdued, what does Moses say they get?

answers.text: They may go home and the land is theirs
They get first pick of land in Canaan
They get to lead every tribe in battle

cards.question: Moses tells the Gadites and Reubenites that if they break this promise, nobody will ever know.

cards.text: Moses tells them they'd be sinning against the LORD, and "your sin will find you out." Sin is like cookie crumbs on your apron, friend: you THINK nobody notices, and EVERYBODY notices.
Then Moses says go ahead, build cities for your little ones and folds for your flocks, but do what you promised. Build the house, friend. Just show up for everybody ELSE'S move.

cards.question: Moses says build, but keep the promise. How do the Gadites and Reubenites answer?

answers.text: They'll do just as Moses commands
They ask for time to think it over
They offer to send half their men

cards.text: Their children, wives and animals will stay in the cities of Gilead, but every man is equipped for war and will cross over to the battle before the LORD. EVERY man, friend, not just whoever's free that weekend.

cards.question: Moses makes the deal official. He gives orders about the Gadites and Reubenites to ___ the priest, ___ son of Nun and the family leaders of the tribes.

cards.text: Moses tells them: if the Gadites and Reubenites cross the Jordan armed for battle and the land is subdued, give them the land of Gilead as a possession. The whole leadership team heard it, friend, so nobody gets to say "I don't remember that."

cards.question: Moses says if the Gadites and Reubenites don't arm up and cross, they get no land at all.
The Gadites and Reubenites reply to Moses that as the ___ has spoken to your servants, so they will do.

cards.text: They'll cross into Canaan armed before the LORD, so their inheritance can be on this side of the Jordan. Deal SEALED, friend, and now Moses hands out the land.

cards.question: Moses gives land east of the Jordan to the Gadites, the Reubenites and the half-tribe of ___.

cards.text: That half-tribe comes from Manasseh son of Joseph, and Moses gives them all the kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og, king of Bashan, with the cities and all the territory around them. Two whole KINGDOMS, friend, and the biggest move I ever made was across the kitchen into a junk drawer.

The Gadites build up Dibon, Ataroth, Jazer and more as fortified cities with folds for their flocks, and the Reubenites build up Heshbon, Nebo and others and rename the cities they rebuild. New owners ALWAYS change something, friend.

cards.question: The descendants of Machir, son of Manasseh, go to Gilead and capture it. Who do they drive out?
Moses gives Gilead to the clan of Machir son of Manasseh, and they settle there.

cards.text: Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, captures villages and calls them Havvoth-jair. JAIR named the villages after JAIR, friend, and I see what you did there.

cards.question: Then Nobah goes and captures Kenath and its villages. What does he call the place?

findings.problem: The question never identifies what "this move" or "it" means. The needed action, discouraging Israel from crossing into the land, appears only on earlier cards. Restate that action so the question stands on its own.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "Do all that" sends the baker back to the conditions on story card 1, which is no longer visible. The question should restate that the Gadites and Reubenites must arm themselves and cross the Jordan for battle.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Marking "they get no land at all" false explains only what does not happen. No card tells the actual outcome in Numbers 32:30: if they do not cross armed, they must accept their possession among the other Israelites in Canaan. This leaves a key part of Moses' agreement untaught.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Immediately after mentioning the half-tribe, the card says "Moses gives them all" the two kingdoms, making it sound as though the half-tribe alone receives them. Numbers 32:33 gives the kingdoms to the Gadites, the Reubenites and the half-tribe of Manasseh together. Name all three recipients.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
